troubleshooting.title: Authentication Fails (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket)
troubleshooting.shortdesc: Most sign-in failures come down to using a password where the server now requires a token.

condition.title: Problem
condition.p: A push, pull, fetch, or clone over HTTPS is rejected with an authentication error, even though your username and password look correct.

cause.title: Cause
cause.p: The server may no longer accept account passwords for Git operations, or your account uses two-factor authentication.

step.cmd: Create a personal access token in your Git server account.

ul.li: GitHub no longer accepts account passwords. Use a personal access token.
Bitbucket app passwords can no longer be created (as of September 9, 2025); create an API token with the required scopes and use it as the password with your Bitbucket username.
If your account uses two-factor authentication, you must use a token rather than your password.

step.cmd: Enter the token when the Git Client prompts you. See .
